About the Department of Higher Education
The Massachusetts Department of Higher Education (DHE) is the staff to the 13-member , responsible for executing the Board's policies and day-to-day operations.

At the Massachusetts Department of Higher Education (DHE),
we share these interconnected values:
Equity Understanding and confronting oppression in all its forms

As a DHE employee, and commit to embody them through continued learning and personal growth:
I aspire to practice these values and behaviors
Equity
I seek to understand, appreciate, and interact with people of all racial, cultural, and social identities, as well as all roles and lived experiences.
I seek to expand my knowledge and analysis of the roles that systems of injustice play in our society, on our campuses, and in our Department by:
participating fully in equity learning and training opportunities;
practicing self-reflection and introspection; and
striving to unlearn my harmful beliefs and behaviors.
I commit to integrating my knowledge and analysis of key racial equity concepts into my work and my interactions.
Accountability
I practice honest and direct communication, and I constructively address issues with colleagues when they arise, no matter how difficult or uncomfortable
I communicate in a timely and respectful manner with all colleagues, from acknowledging and honoring requests to closing loops.
I listen actively, empathetically, and without defensiveness, testing my assumptions and seeking to understand and clarify others’ questions and observations.

I call on myself and my colleagues to stand up and be accountable, follow through on what we promise, communicate clearly when I cannot fulfill commitments, and call attention to what we might fail to
I examine my own work and actions with the same rigor that I examine others’.
I own my mistakes, learn from them, and share my learning with others.
Community
I uphold an environment of , both me and you, and I put people above work.
us
I am mindful of other people’s time, workload, and need for rest, and I show care for everyone’s physical, spiritual, and mental health.
I create and communicate realistic, goal-oriented workplans that identify what is the plan, what success looks like, what is expected for others’ time and contributions, and how this may affect other
I am clear about the urgency of my asks from colleagues, and I welcome my colleagues to ask questions about the work and timelines posed.
I am proactive and mindful in seeking and cherishing the many connections between myself and my colleagues, and how those connections can elevate our sense of trust and community.
Empowerment
I exercise leadership by developing the power, skills, and knowledge of others
I include people affected by decisions and policies in the decision-making and policy-making processes.
I recognize and value all forms of expertise and strengths, and I amplify the voices of others in recognition of their experiences and skills.
I appreciate and develop critical and independent thinkers.
Intentionality
I work deliberatively within ambiguity and recognize there is not only one opinion or one way of thinking.
I do not oversimplify complex issues by reducing them to either/or, right/wrong, or good/bad choices.
I take time to pause, reflect, and plan before acting.
I prioritize collaboration and inclusion above expediency.
I stay open to new ideas and processes to improve the way we do things, in my work and in my field.
Teamwork
I stay informed on, prioritize, and amplify the Department’s shared goals.
I build and sustain authentic, productive working relationships with colleagues across teams, levels, and social identities.
I collaborate and seek multiple opinions and perspectives when problem solving.
I let my team know when I am overwhelmed, and if I know what may help, I ask for it.
I embrace mutually agreed-upon goals and protocols in making decisions as a team, even when my individual approach or preference would be different.
I practice and encourage information sharing within and across teams to support the effectiveness of my colleagues and the Department as a whole.
